svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS DD — Appendix D · AppD_SchwartzBruhat, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,634 declarations of the 144 items on CD, each with its kind, file, line and state; 98 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

g.text: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,634 declarations of the 144 items on CD, each with its kind, file, line and state; 98 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of CD's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card, and under it, in italics, the first sentence of its first declaration's docstring, quoted. Then the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The Pontryagin dual is Hausdorff and locally compact.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This proof assumes a second-countable group and an available Plancherel measure. The Fourier isometries on two distinct cosets would give a nonzero integrable density on their disjoint union with every character integral equal to zero.

g.text: A locally compact Hausdorff abelian group with a continuous homomorphism to a finite-dimensional torus and discrete kernel is locally Euclidean.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This isolates the local chart construction. On a sufficiently small compact identity neighborhood the homomorphism is an embedding. In logarithm coordinates its image near zero is a relatively closed local additive subgroup of a finite-dimensional real vector space, hence locally a linear subspace. Translation gives charts at every point.

g.text: An invariant differential operator preserves Schwartz–Bruhat functions, and on the Fourier side it acts by multiplication by its symbol.

g.text: This is the projector identity described after (D.1.6.26), with the forward transform on both paths and both compact averages taken with mass one. The ill-typed inverse-transform formula (D.1.6.25) is left open.

g.text: The images of the two subgroups of a structural pair in the quotient by a closed subgroup form a structural pair of the quotient.

g.text: The first proof paragraph on p. 776 prints $k'k/k'$ as the compact subgroup in the pair for $G/k$. We use the image $k'k/k$ of $k'$.

g.text: The displayed map on p. 776 averages over $k'k/k'$. The kernel on the source stage $\Gamma'/k'$ is the image $(k\cap\Gamma')k'/k'$.

text.tspan: · p. 807 · 40 declarations, 1 deviating from the print

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The continuous linear comparison from the completed inductive tensor product to the completed projective tensor product is bijective and identifies their bounded subsets.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Every a in I must lie between two test exponents, allowing equality. This includes finite endpoints when they belong to I and handles unbounded intervals.
